QuickMelody.notes: Source read at commit 21bfcbf, the commit whose plugin.json carries the installed 2.0.0. The Max and Min knobs are configured with defaults of -5 and +5 (QuickMelody.cpp:29-30), so the default Max is below the default Min; the output is computed as (max - min) * phase + min at line 103, which simply runs the sweep downward. The Max and Min inputs replace their knobs rather than being added to them.

PolyAutoPan.notes: Source read at commit 21bfcbf, the commit whose plugin.json carries the installed 2.0.0. The Rate input replaces the knob rather than being added to it, and its law (24.995 V + 250.05, PolyAutoPan.cpp:44) is not clamped, so a voltage outside ±10V runs the sweep faster than 500 beats per minute or backwards. WeightedQuantizer.notes: Source read at commit 21bfcbf, the commit whose plugin.json carries the installed 2.0.0. Input index 0 is the C weight and index 1 is the pitch In, so the index order is not the panel order; index 12 is the B weight and index 2 the C sharp weight. A weight CV does not merely override its knob, it writes the value into the knob with setValue (WeightedQuantizer.cpp:83 and the eleven like it), so the knob visibly follows the cable and keeps the last value when the cable is pulled. With every weight at zero the module short-circuits input to output (line 164).

16Squared.notes: Source read at commit 21bfcbf, the commit whose plugin.json carries the installed 2.0.0. The knob values are copied into the store for the current step on every sample (setValues at 16Squared.cpp:112) and copied back out of it whenever the step changes, which is what makes one row of knobs serve all sixteen steps. RomanQuantizer.notes: Source read at commit 21bfcbf, the commit whose plugin.json carries the installed 2.0.0. THE PTTERN INPUT IS DEAD: RomanQuantizer.cpp:403 configures it and nothing in process() ever reads it, so the sequence can only be changed with the knob. The maker's README lists 'Pattrn: Switch between different sequences' without saying which control, and the jack's own tooltip reads 'Pattern', which is why it gets a line saying so rather than being left untagged. The sixteen chord squares are ChordWidget displays with no ParamWidget, so they have no census position and no note; the same is true of the key display under the KEY knob.
